items.title: DEEP Robotics Unveils Five Research Advances in Embodied AI - markets.businessinsider.com
items.summary: BOSTON, Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- DEEP Robotics has unveiled five research advances supporting the development of DEEPRobotics-Brain, its embodied intelligence architecture for real-world robot operation. Spanning physical prediction, navigation and manipulation, policy optimization, predictive memory, and data-driven evaluation, the research addresses a shared challenge: helping robots work reliably in environments that change. The five research areas comprise the DR-WM-1.0 world model, the DR-VLA-2.0 embodied foundation model, the DR-APO policy optimization framework, the DR-Agent embodied agent, and the DR-Benchmark data and evaluation platform. Together, the studies connect physical prediction, navigation and manipulation, policy learning, dynamic memory, and real-world data. The research supports DEEP Robotics’ broader goal of developing robots that can respond to human instructions and practical operating conditions, with capabilities evaluated through simulation, real-robot experiments, and shared benchmarks. items.title: Neura Robotics launches multimodal AI model that gives robots perception and memory - Robotics & Automation News
items.summary: # Neura Robotics launches multimodal AI model that gives robots perception and memory. **Neura Robotics has launched Neuron AI, its multimodal foundation model for physical AI.**. Combining 3D vision, touch, audio, robot state and language with memory, Neuron AI enables robots to act on information beyond what cameras alone can capture, as well as retain relevant context when objects disappear from view. “With Neuron AI, we are building the brain of the physical world: Physical AI that turns human expertise and physical experience into capabilities robots can learn and apply. The additional senses also improve tasks that vision can already handle: in welding, for example, the quality of a seam can be judged from the sound of the process. Real-world robot data: Robots across different embodiments perform tasks in Neura Gyms, Neura’s training infrastructure for cognitive robots and Physical AI and real-world environments, generating synchronized vision, touch, force, audio and movement data.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary: Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] “Robots are advancing quickly, but developing them for real-world environments remains slow, data-intensive and difficult to scale,” Huang said. “Working with UC Berkeley, NVIDIA is helping advance a new approach combining agentic AI, simulation and open industrial task-focused benchmarks to help developers rapidly test and improve robot behavior before deployment.” [...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger.

Abstract
In this work, we develop and release Llama 2, a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned
large language models (LLMs) ranging in scale from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters.

1 Introduction
Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown great promise as highly capable AI assistants that excel in
complex reasoning tasks requiring expert knowledge across a wide range of fields, including in specialized
domains such as programming and creative writing. They enable interaction with humans through intuitive
chat interfaces, which has led to rapid and widespread adoption among the general public.
The capabilities of LLMs are remarkable considering the seemingly straightforward nature of the training
methodology. Auto-regressive transformers are pretrained on an extensive corpus of self-supervised data,
followed by alignment with human preferences via techniques such as Reinforcement Learning with Human
Feedback (RLHF). Although the training methodology is simple, high computational requirements have
limited the development of LLMs to a few players. There have been public releases of pretrained LLMs
(such as BLOOM (Scao et al., 2022), LLaMa-1 (Touvron et al., 2023), and Falcon (Penedo et al., 2023)) that
match the performance of closed pretrained competitors like GPT-3 (Brown et al., 2020) and Chinchilla
(Hoffmann et al., 2022), but none of these models are suitable substitutes for closed “product” LLMs, such
as ChatGPT, BARD, and Claude. These closed product LLMs are heavily fine-tuned to align with human
preferences, which greatly enhances their usability and safety. This step can require significant costs in
compute and human annotation, and is often not transparent or easily reproducible, limiting progress within
the community to advance AI alignment research.
In this work, we develop and release Llama 2, a family of pretrained and fine-tuned LLMs,Llama 2 and
Llama 2-Chat, at scales up to 70B parameters. On the series of helpfulness and safety benchmarks we tested,
Llama 2-Chat models generally perform better than existing open-source models. They also appear to
be on par with some of the closed-source models, at least on the human evaluations we performed (see
Figures 1 and 3). We have taken measures to increase the safety of these models, using safety-specific data
annotation and tuning, as well as conducting red-teaming and employing iterative evaluations. Additionally,
this paper contributes a thorough description of our fine-tuning methodology and approach to improving
LLM safety. We hope that this openness will enable the community to reproduce fine-tuned LLMs and
continue to improve the safety of those models, paving the way for more responsible development of LLMs.
We also share novel observations we made during the development ofLlama 2 and Llama 2-Chat, such as
the emergence of tool usage and t
